checks.label: Investigated once

slate.title: Spawn remediation cards
slate.body: The fee change is not a variance to accept — it is a cost with two possible fixes, each owned by a different flow. Spawning links this bridge to them bidirectionally, so the card that fixes it knows why it exists.

cards.title: Packaging right-size for the 31 reclassified SKUs
cards.detail: Four of the 31 already appear on the dim-weight candidate list. Right-sizing those boxes drops them back under the tier boundary rather than paying the new tier forever.

cards.title: Pass-through check on the residual SKUs
cards.detail: The 27 SKUs that cannot be right-sized need the fee absorbed or passed through. Elasticity and competitive headroom decide which — that is the repricing flow’s question, not this one.

slate.title: Annotate and archive
slate.body: Records what yesterday was, so the same shape next month opens with the answer attached instead of starting a fresh investigation.
slate.note: Aug 18 CM fell $1,840 (14.7%) against the trailing 7-day mean. Amazon revised dimensional-weight tiers effective that day, reclassifying 31 SKUs upward at −$2,210. The 9.11 price slate offset +$610 on its first full day; returns, mix and staged ad bids account for the rest within normal variation. Residual +$130 · 1.0%. Two remediation cards spawned — packaging right-size and pass-through check. This is a recurring daily cost until one of them lands.

slate.title: Adjust the contract band
slate.body: The band decides which days raise a card at all. Tightening it surfaces smaller moves and more of them; widening it means days like yesterday pass unremarked.

slate.title: Escalate with the bridge attached
slate.body: For when the fix needs someone outside this flow. The recipient gets the waterfall, the classifier output and the drill rows — not a summary of them.
